tier_rows.description: Page bound of the tier index read: how many tier rows one selection may consider.

model_rows.description: Page bound of the active-model read: how many catalog rows one selection ranks over.

description.purpose: The lookup: a request names REQUIREMENTS (a tier, capabilities, a cost ceiling, a context floor) and the answer is a resolution -- one model id with its provider, wire dialect, window and price, plus the reason code that produced it. Every step is a comparison against catalog rows; the rank `cost_out asc, cost_in asc, context_window desc, model_id asc` is total, so the same request over the same catalog resolves the same way forever.
description.use_when: As the read port of the registry. Ask it before wiring a cell, or from an agent as a tool: `which tier handles vision under 5 cents` is a filter, not a judgement. A named tier is an index lookup; a request without a tier is a ranked search over the active models.
description.not_in_scope: It never guesses. Requirements nothing satisfies come back `resolved: false` with a reason code and NO model id -- there is no nearest match and no default, because a wrong model returned confidently is worse than no answer. It sends nothing to anybody either: resolving is not remapping, that is `./hand` and only on call. And it cannot tell a cell what it is running today -- a cell cannot be read, only pushed to.
description.emits_meaning: route answer: the resolution as a tool_result, with hop.resolved / hop.reason_code / hop.model_id / hop.tier so a parent edge can fork without opening the body. route rstore: its own two catalog reads and the one journal line. route error: the store refused an op, or the request was not a tool_call turn carrying JSON.
description.consumes_meaning: context.lr_phase and context.lr_carry are the lane's state -- a code cell has no cell.db, so the request rides the store round trip. context.asker is edge truth and becomes the cell_path of the journal line.
examples: {"tier":"mid"} -> resolved: the model the tier index points at, reason_code tier_active
{"tier":"light","capability":"vision"} -> resolved: false, tier_below_requirement -- the tier is the answer or there is none
{"capability":["tools","vision"],"max_cost":500} -> the cheapest active model that has both, reason_code ranked
{"max_cost":1} -> resolved: false, no_candidate, model_id "" -- and one resolutions row saying so
